literal_meaning: ঝেড়ে কাপড় পরিয়ে দেওয়া (shaking off dust from clothes and making someone wear them)
figurative_meaning_en: To annoy or pester someone persistently
similar_in_english: To drive someone up the wall
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে তার ছোট ভাইকে ঝেড়ে কাপড় পড়ানোর মতো বিরক্ত করছে।
মা সারাদিন ছেলেকে নাজেহাল করে ঝেড়ে কাপড় পড়ানোর মতো অনুরোধ করলেন।
example_sentences_in_english: He is annoying his little brother like making him wear shaken clothes.
Mom pestered her son all day, just like forcing him into freshly shaken clothes.
history: This idiom likely originates from rural Bengali practices of shaking dust off clothes before wearing them, symbolizing unnecessary hassle or irritation in everyday chores.
note: The expression evokes a sense of futile or bothersome action, common in Bengali oral tradition.
